solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Measured carpet at end of store

indicators.note: 'at end of' tells you where to set the second piece

blocks.note: a deli is a food store
to carpet someone is to tell them off

explanation.surface: Someone measures a carpet in the back of a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Measured' and 'carpet' pose as flooring talk; carpet here is the verb, as in being carpeted by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: measured steps or words are slow and considered, done on purpose.

clue.text: Climbing tree in drought exhausted stray

indicators.note: in a down entry a word that climbs is read from bottom to top, so it comes out reversed
'in' asks for one piece to sit within the other
something exhausted has been drained of its contents, so the word keeps only its shell

explanation.surface: A tree clings on in a drought while something wanders off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing tree' reads naturally as a tree to climb; it is a fir growing upwards in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: cattle or thoughts that wander from their course are said to do this.

clue.text: City of Crete lies in ruins

indicators.note: something in ruins has been knocked down, so the letters must be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A city on Crete lies in ruins, like Knossos.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to an ancient Cretan city such as Knossos; the answer is an English city in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: this is a cathedral city in the English East Midlands.

clue.text: Maladroit Pat possibly OK carrying good wine

indicators.note: 'possibly' signals an example
to carry something is to hold it within you

blocks.note: a pat is a small portion of butter

explanation.surface: A clumsy man called Pat, happily carrying some good wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat looks like a person's name; it is a pat of butter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone clumsy who keeps dropping things.

clue.text: Pick up fool daughter’s left for Romeo

blocks.note: NATO alphabet, put in its place

explanation.surface: A father's daughter has jilted her fool of a boyfriend for a Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo seems to be the new lover; it is just the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to pick up a parcel, a guest or a radio signal is to get it.

clue.text: Hard time keeping Henry in meditation

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it

blocks.note: the henry is the unit of inductance, symbol H

explanation.surface: Henry has a hard time trying to meditate.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUGH and T run together as TOUGHT, and the H slips in after the first T.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: meditation is the act of reflecting, of careful contemplation.

clue.text: Key teacher perhaps unwilling to leave pit?

blocks.note: Bachelor of Education, the degree many teachers hold

explanation.surface: A key teacher refuses to leave the orchestra pit.
explanation.walkthrough: Pit is British slang for your bed; the question mark flags a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom-based definition: pit is slang for your bed, so staying in it means still lying there.

clue.text: Take the bait delivered for bay

indicators.note: a delivered speech is spoken aloud, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: a fish that takes the bait bites

explanation.surface: A fish takes the bait out in the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Australian Bight is the best-known example of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A geographical term: a wide curve in a coastline forming an open bay.

clue.text: Sack of small fish Barb’s taken east

blocks.note: a barb is a dig, a cutting remark; the ’s is 'has'
the char is a trout-like fish
standard abbreviation, added at the end

explanation.surface: A sack of little fish that Barb has taken off to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Barb looks like a woman's name, or even a fish in this fishy surface; it is a dig, and Barb's means 'Barb has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to sack an employee is to dismiss them from the job.

clue.text: Label new trees English chief maybe surveys

explanation.surface: An English chief labels new trees while surveying woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: Arch as a prefix means chief (archbishop, arch-enemy), which is why it can stand for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the questionnaires firms send out to learn what customers want.

clue.text: Crazy notion, half rejected by setter of The Listener

indicators.note: to reject half is to throw out one of the two halves, leaving the other
'by' in its sense 'beside' sets the next piece next to it

blocks.note: IDEA losing its second half, EA
the setter refers to himself as I
otic means of the ear, the listening organ

explanation.surface: A mad idea gets thrown out by the compiler of The Listener crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famous crossword series, so 'setter of The Listener' reads as one person; it splits into I plus OTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something so foolish it seems mad.

clue.text: Limits wearing really large shades

indicators.note: clothes worn go round you

blocks.note: limits, as in the range of a gun

explanation.surface: Someone is wearing really big sunglasses, pushing the limits.
explanation.walkthrough: Shades suggests sunglasses; here it is colours. OS (outsize) is the size label on extra-large clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: several hues at the warm end of the spectrum, like tangerine and amber.

clue.text: Supporter close to battle inside Hertfordshire town about to fall?

indicators.note: the close of something is its end

blocks.note: a golf tee supports the ball
Tring is a small market town in Hertfordshire

explanation.surface: A supporter near the fighting inside a Hertfordshire town, ready to fall.
explanation.walkthrough: TEE stands first, then TRING takes E to give TERING. The question mark marks 'about to fall' as a description, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Description, flagged by the question mark: wobbling unsteadily on the brink of toppling over.

clue.text: Drawing failing to show son’s craft

indicators.note: something that fails to show is missing

explanation.surface: A drawing that fails to show a son's craftsmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: Craft here is a boat, not a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft in the sense of vessel: this is a two-masted sailing boat.

clue.text: Tailor wheeled on second design

indicators.note: a wheel turns round, so a wheeled word is turned back to front
in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A tailor wheels on a second design.
explanation.walkthrough: Tailor is a verb here: to tailor a suit is to fit it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a recurring pattern or figure in art or decoration.

clue.text: Notes Roman mead that’s distributed

indicators.note: things distributed are spread about, so the letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: Notes about how mead was shared out in Roman times.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a Latin plural, which suits the Roman surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: written notes and reminders, using the Latin plural.

clue.text: Gallery enthralled by Cliff on electronic vehicle

indicators.note: to be enthralled is to be held captive
in an across clue, placing a piece on another means it follows it

blocks.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff

explanation.surface: A gallery goer captivated by Cliff Richard singing on an electronic track.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff looks like Cliff Richard; it is a scar, a rocky cliff face.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a British term for a station wagon, a long-backed car.

clue.text: Guy abridged popular post providing early coverage for those in theatre

definitions.text: providing early coverage for those in theatre

indicators.note: an abridged text is cut short

explanation.surface: A man's shortened popular post gives early reviews of a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre suggests the stage and coverage suggests reviews, but it is the theatre of war and coverage is protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the linked-ring armour worn by medieval soldiers in a theatre of war.

clue.text: Boomer in guesthouse covers options on trolley?

indicators.note: 'in' here means the answer lies within the words that follow
the words cover the answer, concealing it inside them like a lid

explanation.surface: A baby boomer in a guesthouse weighs up the options on the dessert trolley.
explanation.walkthrough: A dessert trolley is wheeled round restaurant tables; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: sweets one might pick from a restaurant dessert trolley.

clue.text: Boorish group losing leader edges away

indicators.note: a word that loses its leader drops its first letter
to edge something is to border it

blocks.note: a bunch is a group, minus B

explanation.surface: A rude gang loses its leader and slowly edges away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges away' reads as a phrasal verb; edges is the container and away is OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe coarse, ill-mannered behaviour.

clue.text: Ruler binding back of right arm

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so its final letter

blocks.note: a shogun was a military ruler of Japan

explanation.surface: A ruler binds the back of his right arm.
explanation.walkthrough: Arm looks like a limb; it is a weapon, a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: Arm in the sense of weapon: a firearm with a long barrel for firing shot.

clue.text: Get round hull of drone after spacewalk?

indicators.note: a hull is the outer shell

blocks.note: EVA = extravehicular activity, NASA's term for a spacewalk

explanation.surface: An astronaut on a spacewalk circles the hull of a drone.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that EVA is a spacewalk only in NASA jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to get round a rule or tax is to dodge or elude it.

clue.text: Bank backing for one director

indicators.note: to back is to move in reverse, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: director shortened to its first three letters

explanation.surface: A bank is backing one of its directors.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is finance, but the bank is a raised strip of earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a long raised strip of earth or snow is a bank.

clue.text: Funds party that’s distasteful

blocks.note: what you say at something distasteful

explanation.surface: Funds for a party that some find distasteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' could be a political party with funds; it is just a do.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: in informal English, money is often called bread or this.

clue.text: Tight finish, Charlie declared

indicators.note: a declared thing is spoken aloud, so the word is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: a charlie is a fool, a nit

explanation.surface: Charlie announces a tight finish to a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is British slang for a fool (a right charlie), and nit is another word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tight group is closely bound together.

clue.text: Character taking heart at first pilot’s forecast?

indicators.note: 'at first' picks the opening letter of each word it follows

blocks.note: first letters of taking and heart

explanation.surface: A pilot takes heart at the start of the forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking heart' tempts a solver to use a middle letter, but here 'at first' applies to both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Character in the sense of letter: the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Modern split oven coating uranium and gold

indicators.note: a coating goes round what it covers

explanation.surface: A modern oven with a coating of uranium and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The NOVE shell opens between NO and VE for the U, then gold's symbol AU ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing: the word for new, as in art nouveau, the modern style of 1900.

clue.text: Refuse game sent to port at start of season

indicators.note: port is a ship's left side, so in an across clue the word travels leftwards, reversed

blocks.note: brag is a card game, ancestor of poker
to season something is to mature it, to age it

explanation.surface: Rejected, the game is sent to port at the start of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse and season both look like verbs; refuse is rubbish and season means to age, as with timber or cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: refuse, stressed on the first syllable, is rubbish.

clue.text: Group separated by grand commander

blocks.note: a-ha, the Norwegian pop group behind Take On Me

explanation.surface: A pop group splits up because of a grand commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Group suggests a military unit next to commander; it is the band a-ha.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical title: an Ottoman military commander or chief officer.

clue.text: Cool mate smuggles fur

indicators.note: a smuggler hides goods inside

blocks.note: china plate, rhyming slang for mate

explanation.surface: A cool friend smuggles furs through customs.
explanation.walkthrough: China for mate is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by source: the soft grey pelt of a South American rodent, prized for coats.
